analysis: What changed vs the 5 AM brief: the tape cooled slightly from its early highs — futures went from S&P +0.25% / Dow +0.29% / Nasdaq +0.46% at 07:35 ET to +0.19% / +0.32% / +0.27% at 06:56 ET, still green but no longer accelerating. The fresh macro input, September durable goods (+1.8% headline, beating consensus), is a mild positive that markets are mostly looking past: core orders (+0.5%) and the business-spending proxy (core capital goods +0.5%) both slightly missed, and the AI-spend proxy inside the report actually dipped. The real overnight story is the AI supply chain proving demand again: Celestica's blowout (revenue +83%, 2027 guide of $40B vs $35.5B consensus) plus Cadence's beat-and-raise reframes Monday's Anthropic-led rebound as demand-backed, not just multiple expansion — though Goldman's note that the debate is now about the cost of capital, not demand, is the right frame for the week. HSBC's miss is the counterweight: banks are the tape's drag this morning. Signal: durable goods split (headline beat, core miss), Celestica/Cadence demand prints, futures levels, HSBC drag, the 10 a.m. ET confidence and home-sales prints. Noise: the micro-cap premarket gainers (BRAI +43-48% with no catalyst), the Anthropic fast-entry index-buying chatter (mechanical, weeks away at earliest), and the SK Hynix special-dividend report (still single-source, unconfirmed). The open inherits a green but fragile tape with two live data prints still to come before the bell settles.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: US stock futures stayed higher into the open but cooled from early highs: at 06:56 ET, Dow E-minis were up 169 points (+0.32%), S&P 500 E-minis up 15 points (+0.19%), and Nasdaq 100 E-minis up 79 points (+0.27%), versus +0.25% / +0.29% / +0.46% at 07:35 ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: The open still inherits upward momentum, but the fade from the morning's best levels shows buyers are not chasing ahead of the 10 a.m. ET data and the Fed decision.

headlines.headline: September durable goods orders rose 1.8% month-on-month to $345.4B, topping the +1.4% consensus and rebounding from August's +0.1%; but core orders (ex-transport) rose only 0.5% vs +0.6% expected, and core capital goods orders — the business equipment proxy — rose 0.5% vs +0.7% expected, moderating from +1.6% prior.
headlines.why_it_matters: A headline beat with a soft core — the report supports the economy-holding read without giving the Fed a reason to move, so it is unlikely to reset the tape on its own.

headlines.headline: Celestica surged 15-17% in premarket trading (one later read put it above 26% in extended hours) after Q3 revenue jumped 83% to $5.83B and adjusted EPS of $3.30 beat the $2.96 estimate; it raised its 2026 outlook and guided to $40B of 2027 revenue, up 90% and above the $35.5B consensus, citing an AI infrastructure 'supercycle' and stronger 2028 customer demand.
headlines.why_it_matters: The strongest demand print of the week so far — a 2027 guide far above consensus supports the AI-hardware leg of the tape into the MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN prints.

headlines.headline: Cadence Design Systems, an Nvidia partner, also beat expectations and raised its full-year forecast, rising about 2% premarket; Micron, Broadcom, Lumentum and Astera Labs rose alongside it.
headlines.why_it_matters: Two independent AI-supply-chain beats in one morning — demand, not just sentiment, is carrying the chip complex into the open.

headlines.headline: HSBC slid about 6.9% premarket after Q3 pretax profit of $9.63B missed expectations despite a new $1B buyback, with narrowing margins and potential UK windfall taxes in focus; it was the premarket's biggest drag from the banking sector.
headlines.why_it_matters: Banks are the tape's offset this morning — a big-bank miss keeps the rally narrow and gives bears a sector to point to if the open fades.

headlines.headline: JetBlue's relief rally extended, up over 10% premarket after it reported a day early with widening losses but reaffirmed guidance, a day after shares hit an all-time low on reports senior creditors hired a restructuring adviser.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance reaffirmed beats bankruptcy chatter for a session — a relief bounce, not a fundamental repair, so it fades fast if the 10 a.m. call disappoints.

headlines.headline: Nvidia was up less than 1% premarket and Meta slightly lower after Nvidia confirmed its $3B investment in Meta's equity offering and the deeper Muse partnership; Jefferies noted Magnificent 7 earnings growth could trail the rest of the S&P 500 (21% vs 32%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The deal is now priced in and the tape has moved on to earnings — NVDA/META need the hyperscaler prints, not more deal headlines, to move from here.

headlines.headline: Tesla climbed over 1% premarket, adding to Monday's 5.2% jump after Barclays upgraded the stock to overweight, citing a possible SpaceX combination and stronger core operations.
headlines.why_it_matters: A second day of upgrade-driven strength — TSLA is the megacap with its own catalyst this morning rather than riding the AI tape.

headlines.headline: Oil eased further: WTI futures were down about 0.7% near $101.05 and Brent slipped for a second day as Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan-Iran talks in Tehran competed with supply-disruption risk; gold futures fell 0.4% to $4,025 an ounce and bitcoin slipped below $80,000. The 10-year Treasury yield ticked lower to 4.98% from 4.99%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Crude's pullback from six-week highs eases one inflation input into the Fed meeting, and a lower 10-year keeps the rate backdrop benign into the open.

headlines.headline: The Fed's two-day meeting begins today, decision due Wednesday 2:00 p.m. ET with Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 2:30 p.m. ET; markets price only about an 11% chance of a hike this week after September's increase. Still ahead today: S&P/Case-Shiller home prices (9:00 a.m. ET), consumer confidence and new-home sales (10:00 a.m. ET), plus a $70B note auction.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hold is priced, so the 10 a.m. ET confidence and home-sales prints are the last fresh macro inputs before Wednesday — they set the tone for the open's second hour.

headlines.headline: Carried forward: Apple has acknowledged inner-display cracking on a small number of iPhone Duo units after its Oct 23 launch, with no failure rate given; Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees two days before its fiscal Q1 print Wednesday after the close.
headlines.why_it_matters: Neither story produced a fresh headline this hour, but both are live overhangs into the open — Duo reports widening, or MSFT's buyout framing, would move their tapes fast.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Prior regular session (Mon Oct 26): advancers ahead 1.36:1, but the bounce leaned on the AI complex rather than the whole list. Technology (XLK +1.72%) was the best sector and semiconductors (SMH +2.74%) led; Communication Services (XLC -1.57%) was the worst sector, dragged by Meta. Volume vs 20-day average was not shown in checked sources — left null, not estimated.
market_snapshot.notes: Tue Oct 27, 6:00 AM PT — 30 minutes before the 6:30 AM PT open. Futures are the 06:56 ET Reuters read (S&P +0.19%, Dow +0.32%, Nasdaq +0.27%), cooled from the 07:35 ET read (+0.25% / +0.29% / +0.46%). Prior session closes: S&P 500 7,676.77 (+0.70%), Nasdaq Composite 26,169 (+0.82%), Dow 52,361.58 (+0.28%). VIX 18.39 is Monday's close, down from Friday's 19.45. 10-year yield 4.98%, ticked lower from 4.99% (one separate markets roundup put Monday's close at 5.00% on official Treasury par-yield data — the Investopedia read is used here).

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. The Q3 distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield) went ex-dividend Monday Oct 26 and pays Nov 6. Q3 earnings arrive before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 a.m. ET call. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. Background: on Oct 1 the partnership issued 34.5M non-convertible Class A units at a fixed 9.25% annual distribution rate in an internal reorganization, and it now trades on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) after moving from NYSE on Oct 5. WTI easing toward $101.05 keeps crude near six-week highs, so the energy backdrop for compression demand stays supportive with no company-specific catalyst.

watch_next: 10:00 a.m. ET today: consumer confidence (expected ~81.0) and new-home sales (expected ~653K) — the last macro before Wednesday's Fed decision.
After the close today: Visa (est. EPS $3.43) and Robinhood (est. $0.56), plus Seagate and NXP.
Wednesday Oct 28, 2:00 p.m. ET: FOMC decision + Warsh press conference, with Microsoft (fiscal Q1, est. $4.82) and Alphabet (est. $3.11) reporting after the close the same day.
Thursday Oct 29: Amazon reports after the close (est. $2.00), alongside advance Q3 GDP and September PCE prices.
Celestica/Cadence: whether the AI-hardware demand prints hold their premarket gains through the open or fade into the hyperscaler prints.
Meta offering: whether the priced $25B common offering and chipmaker participation steady the stock, or the dilution overhang extends.
Apple Duo: whether crack reports widen beyond a small number or stay contained.
USAC: Q3 earnings before the open Tue Nov 3; $0.525 distribution payable Nov 6.
